newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on peso, capital flow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on peso, capital flow.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 125 basis points to 21.75 percent on Wednesday on a firm peso and foreign capital flowing into Mexico, traders said.
"Funds are still flowing in. The outlook for the year is good so dealers are still interested in Mexican paper," a trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 0.55 of a centavo firmer at 7.7880/7.7940 per dollar.
Traders noted the peso firmed up despite falls in primary rates, as the changes were minimal.

"The atmosphere is generally good. (Primary) rates fell a hair, the peso responded very well and players who had been trying to jack up rates in recent sessions stopped doing so today," a dealer said.
At Tuesday night's primary auction, rates on bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury Certificates) declined by just five basis points to 22.93 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed the session down 75 basis points to 23.75 percent.
Banco de Mexico drained 734 million pesos of excess liquidity from the market by offering an auction to purchase paper in the secondary market, which it assigned overnight at a rate of 23.67 percent.

Liquidity of some 8.7 billion pesos is expected to flow back into the system from recent secondary auctions. Traders said the resulting liquidity surplus would be trimmed by an oversupply of 1.309 billion pesos cariied over from the primary auction.
